sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔。

sentences.en: In Chinese mythology, Meng Po is sometimes known as the goddess of oblivion.
sentences.zh: 在中国神话中，孟婆有时被称为遗忘女神。

sentences.en: She polices the land of the dead and has a special responsibility.
sentences.zh: 她巡视死者的国度，并肩负着一项特殊的职责。

sentences.en: She makes sure that souls on their way to being reincarnated do not remember their past lives.
sentences.zh: 她要确保那些即将转世投胎的灵魂不记得他们过去的生平。

sentences.en: To ensure this, she prepares a soup with five ingredients.
sentences.zh: 为了确保这一点，她用五种成分熬制了一种汤。

sentences.en: Her five-flavored soup of oblivion produces immediate and permanent amnesia.
sentences.zh: 她那五味俱全的忘情汤能让人产生即刻且永久的失忆。

sentences.en: The soul can now proceed to be reincarnated with no memory of previous lives.
sentences.zh: 这样灵魂就能带着对前世毫无记忆的状态去转世投胎了。

sentences.en: There are rare occasions when spirits fail to drink the five-flavored soup,
sentences.zh: 极少数情况下，会有灵体未能喝下这五味汤，

sentences.en: and when these souls are reincarnated, they become humans who can remember their past lives.
sentences.zh: 而当这些灵魂转世时，他们就会成为能够记起前世的人。

sentences.en: Nearly every culture in the world has stories and legends about memory and forgetfulness.
sentences.zh: 世界上几乎每一种文化都有关于记忆和遗忘的故事与传说。

sentences.en: Our ability to remember long-ago events is a signature accomplishment of the brain.
sentences.zh: 我们记住长久以前发生的事情的能力是大脑的一项标志性成就。

sentences.en: Our inability to remember important things is an endless source of frustration.
sentences.zh: 我们记不住重要事情的无能则是挫折感的无尽之源。

sentences.en: Today on the show, and in a companion story on Hidden Brain Plus,
sentences.zh: 今天在节目中，以及在“隐藏的大脑Plus”的配套故事中，

sentences.en: we examine the science of forgetting.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨遗忘的科学。

sentences.en: We look at why our minds hold on to some memories for a lifetime,
sentences.zh: 我们来看看为什么我们的大脑能把某些记忆保留一辈子，

sentences.en: but discard others within seconds.
sentences.zh: 却在几秒钟内丢弃另一些记忆。

sentences.en: And we answer a question many people ask themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们要回答许多人经常问自己的一个问题。

sentences.en: Is my forgetfulness a sign that something is wrong with me?
sentences.zh: 我的健忘是不是我出了问题的征兆？

sentences.en: Forgetting to remember, and remembering to forget,
sentences.zh: 忘记去记住，以及记住去忘记，

sentences.en: this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: In Charles Dickens' novel, Great Expectations,
sentences.zh: 在查尔斯·狄更斯的的小说《远大前程》中，

sentences.en: we are introduced to the character Miss Havisham.
sentences.zh: 我们认识了郝薇香小姐这个角色。

sentences.en: Many years earlier, she was jilted at the altar on her wedding day.
sentences.zh: 许多年前，她在婚礼当天被新郎在圣坛前抛弃。

sentences.en: She becomes obsessed with this moment and cannot move on from it.
sentences.zh: 她对这一刻变得痴迷，无法从中走出来。

sentences.en: She surrounds herself with reminders of that day,
sentences.zh: 她的周围环绕着那天的种种回忆，

sentences.en: wearing her wedding dress and keeping the clock stopped
sentences.zh: 穿着她的婚纱，让时钟停在

sentences.en: at the exact moment of her wedding.
sentences.zh: 她婚礼的那一分那一秒。

sentences.en: In so doing, she becomes consumed with sadness.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，她被悲伤吞噬了。

sentences.en: She becomes a prisoner of her own memories.
sentences.zh: 她成了自己记忆的囚徒。

sentences.en: The memories we carry say a lot about who we are and how we see the world.
sentences.zh: 我们承载的记忆很大程度上说明了我们是谁以及我们如何看待世界。

sentences.en: At University College Dublin,
sentences.zh: 在都柏林大学学院，

sentences.en: psychologist Keira Green studies how memories are formed
sentences.zh: 心理学家凯拉·格林研究记忆是如何形成的，

sentences.en: and the roles that both remembering and forgetting play in our lives.
sentences.zh: 以及记住和遗忘在我们的生活中分别扮演什么角色。

sentences.en: Keira Green, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 凯拉·格林，欢迎来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Hi Shankar, thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 嗨，香卡，谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Keira, I want to talk about something that happened to you some time ago.
sentences.zh: 凯拉，我想聊聊不久前发生在你身上的一件事。

sentences.en: You live in Dublin and it's common for people to get around by bike.
sentences.zh: 你住在都柏林，人们骑自行车出行很常见。

sentences.en: You were riding your bike on the way to a piano lesson.
sentences.zh: 你当时正骑着自行车去上钢琴课。

sentences.en: Can you describe the day for me?
sentences.zh: 你能为我描述一下那天的情况吗？

sentences.en: Sure, it was about three years ago and it was a rainy November night.
sentences.zh: 当然，大约是三年前的一个雨夜，十一月。

sentences.en: And it was dark and it was starting to rain
sentences.zh: 天很黑，而且开始下雨了，

sentences.en: and it was just a kind of cold, miserable night.
sentences.zh: 总之是一个又冷又糟糕的夜晚。

sentences.en: And I was leaving work to go to my piano lesson and I was in a rush.
sentences.zh: 我正离开公司去上钢琴课，当时赶时间。

sentences.en: So, you know, I rushed down the stairs and I got down to my bike
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我匆忙下楼，来到我的自行车旁，

sentences.en: and I realised I'd forgotten my helmet.
sentences.zh: 然后我意识到我忘带头盔了。

sentences.en: So I rushed back upstairs and all the way back up through this very large building
sentences.zh: 所以我又急忙跑回楼上，穿过这栋非常大的建筑跑了回去，

sentences.en: and got my helmet, went back down.
sentences.zh: 拿到了头盔，又跑了下去。

sentences.en: So then I was running late for my lessons.
sentences.zh: 所以当时我去上课已经迟到了。

sentences.en: Keira started zipping through the night to her class.
sentences.zh: 凯拉开始在夜色中飞驰去上课。

sentences.en: The roads were slick.
sentences.zh: 路面很湿滑。

sentences.en: I was cycling through Donnybrook, which is a kind of a busy road.
sentences.zh: 我骑车穿过多尼布鲁克，那是一条比较繁忙的路。

sentences.en: And on that road, there's a lot of buses, there's a lot of cars, there's a lot of cyclists.
sentences.zh: 在那条路上，有很多公交车，有很多汽车，有很多骑自行车的人。

sentences.en: And what there isn't on that part of the road is a bicycle lane.
sentences.zh: 而那段路没有的是一条自行车道。

sentences.en: The bicycle lane had stopped earlier.
sentences.zh: 自行车道在前面就已经断了。

sentences.en: So in fact, as I was cycling along, I was weaving around traffic and in around buses.
sentences.zh: 所以事实上，当我骑车前行时，我在车流中穿梭，在公交车周围绕来绕去。

sentences.en: So I was cycling on wet roads.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在湿滑的路面上骑车。

sentences.en: It's going too faSt.
sentences.zh: 速度太快了。

sentences.en: And you can probably see where this is going
sentences.zh: 你大概能猜到接下来会发生什么

sentences.en: because I skidded on the bike and I skidded right in front of a bus,
sentences.zh: 因为我的自行车打滑了，而且正好滑到了一辆公交车前面，

sentences.en: which fortunately didn't hit me.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是它没有撞到我。

sentences.en: But it was one of those e-bikes, an electric bike.
sentences.zh: 但那是一辆电动自行车。

sentences.en: So it has, you know, the electric power in it, which means it's very heavy.
sentences.zh: 所以它有，你知道的，内置的电力，这意味着它非常重。

sentences.en: The down tube is really heavy.
sentences.zh: 下管真的很重。

sentences.en: So as I fell, my leg got caught in the down tube and snapped my leg in half.
sentences.zh: 所以当我摔倒时，我的腿卡在了下管里，把我的腿当场折断了。

sentences.en: It's like if you could imagine a little small bunch of twigs
sentences.zh: 就像你能想象的一小束细树枝，

sentences.en: and then you snap those twigs.
sentences.zh: 然后你把那些树枝折断。

sentences.en: They don't snap cleanly.
sentences.zh: 它们不是干净利落地断掉。

sentences.en: They snap with shards.
sentences.zh: 断裂处满是碎片。

sentences.en: And I had this very strange experience where I, you know,
sentences.zh: 我当时有这种非常奇怪的经历，你知道的，

sentences.en: I've heard of this happening before, but I'd never experienced it,
sentences.zh: 我听说过这种事发生，但我从未亲自经历过，

sentences.en: where I didn't feel the pain straight away.
sentences.zh: 那就是我没有立刻感觉到疼痛。

sentences.en: I was lying on the ground and, you know, you get that moment of shock.
sentences.zh: 我躺在地上，你知道的，你会经历那一刻的休克。

sentences.en: And I was lying on the ground and I tried to stand up and I couldn't stand up.
sentences.zh: 我躺在地上，试着站起来，却站不起来。

sentences.en: And I didn't know why I couldn't stand up.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么自己站不起来。

sentences.en: And then I looked down and my shoe had come off somewhere.
sentences.zh: 然后我低头一看，我的鞋子不知道掉到哪儿去了。

sentences.en: I don't know where it had gone.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它去哪了。

sentences.en: My shoe had come off, but my leg was dangling like a stuffed sock.
sentences.zh: 我的鞋子掉了，但我的腿像个塞满东西的袜子一样晃晃悠悠地挂着。

sentences.en: The bus driver came rushing out and he was like, are you OK?
sentences.zh: 公交车司机匆忙跑过来，问道：你没事吧？

sentences.en: And I was like, well, no, I think I broke my leg.
sentences.zh: 我说：呃，不好，我想我把腿摔断了。

sentences.en: But it still didn't hurt.
sentences.zh: 但它依然不痛。

sentences.en: And then it was only a little while later that the pain started to come in.
sentences.zh: 直到过了一会儿，疼痛才开始袭来。

sentences.en: The bus driver called 999.
sentences.zh: 公交车司机拨打了999。

sentences.en: So we called the emergency services.
sentences.zh: 于是我们呼叫了紧急救援服务。

sentences.en: But it took nearly an hour for the ambulance to get there because it was a very busy, wet evening.
sentences.zh: 但救护车花了将近一个小时才赶到，因为那是极其繁忙且下雨的傍晚。

sentences.en: So it was snarled up in traffic.
sentences.zh: 所以被堵在车流中了。

sentences.en: As Ciara waited in the rain for the ambulance to fight its way through traffic,
sentences.zh: 当基拉在雨中等待救护车在车流中艰难前行时，

sentences.en: she started to experience the kind of pain she had never dreamed possible.
sentences.zh: 她开始经历她做梦也想不到的那种痛苦。

sentences.en: This incredibly sharp, overwhelming, almost electric pain.
sentences.zh: 这种极其尖锐、排山倒海、几乎带有触电般的剧痛。

sentences.en: And I suppose it's because it's nerve pain, essentially.
sentences.zh: 我想这基本上是因为它是神经痛。

sentences.en: It's the shards of the bone sawing against the nerve.
sentences.zh: 那是骨头碎片在锯着神经。

sentences.en: I've never had the experience before where I would actually scream with pain, but not intend to.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有过这种经历，竟然会痛得大喊大叫，而且并非出于本意。

sentences.en: It was completely involuntary.
sentences.zh: 那是完全不受控制的。

sentences.en: I'd feel like screams were being drawn out of me against my will.
sentences.zh: 我感觉尖叫声是不由自主地从我体内被抽离出来的。

sentences.en: Just incredibly agonising, like electrifyingly sharp, overwhelming, blinding pain.
sentences.zh: 简直痛苦万分，就像触电般尖锐、排山倒海、让人眼前一黑的剧痛。

sentences.en: You know in a hospital where they ask you, you know, like, how's the pain on a scale of 1 to 10?
sentences.zh: 你知道在医院里他们会问你，比如，从1到10分，疼痛程度是多少？

sentences.en: My previous 10 was now a 6 on the broken leg scale of 1 to 10.
sentences.zh: 我以前认为的10分，在断腿的1到10分疼痛量表上现在只能算6分。

sentences.en: Around midnight, doctors decided to try and set the leg.
sentences.zh: 午夜左右，医生决定尝试为她接骨。

sentences.en: They told Ciara they would give her anaesthesia.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉基拉会给她进行麻醉。

sentences.en: I'm allergic to one of the most common anaesthetic.
sentences.zh: 我对最常见的一种麻醉剂过敏。

sentences.en: So they said, we'll try ketamine.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，我们试试氯胺酮。

sentences.en: I'd never had ketamine before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未用过氯胺酮。

sentences.en: And I'm sure if you're taking this for recreational purposes, that maybe it's a good time.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，如果你是为了消遣目的而服用这个，那也许是个好时光。

sentences.en: If you're starting out in a happy state and you're comfortable and relaxed with friends.
sentences.zh: 如果你一开始就处于快乐的状态，并且和朋友在一起感到舒适放松的话。

sentences.en: But if you're starting out in a state of fear and pain, it was terrifying.
sentences.zh: 但如果你一开始就处于恐惧和痛苦的状态中，那就太可怕了。

sentences.en: It was a really, really terrifying experience.
sentences.zh: 那真是一次非常非常可怕的经历。

sentences.en: It felt like it lasted about a thousand years.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像持续了大约一千年。

sentences.en: It was, I, you know, had this incredibly vivid hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道的，产生了极其生动的幻觉。

sentences.en: And I, you know, came to believe at one point that like I had ceased to exist, that I no longer existed.
sentences.zh: 而且我，你知道的，一度开始相信我已经不复存在了，我已经不存在了。

sentences.en: And I could, I could feel not pain, but pressure, which obviously in retrospect was pressure on my leg as I tried to set it.
sentences.zh: 我能，我能感觉到的不是痛感，而是压力，事后回想起来，那显然是他们试图接骨时对我腿施加的压力。

sentences.en: But it felt to me like I was being compressed through, I felt like I was a train being compressed through a train tunnel.
sentences.zh: 但在我感觉看来，我正被压缩着穿过，我感觉自己像一列火车正被压缩着穿过一条火车隧道。

sentences.en: And it was, it was this really, really surreal and very frightening experience.
sentences.zh: 而且那，那真是一次非常非常超现实且极其吓人的经历。

sentences.en: And I've had a lot of flashbacks to that experience since.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，我对那次经历有过很多闪回。

sentences.en: And then after all that, it didn't work.
sentences.zh: 然后在经历了这一切之后，它失败了。

sentences.en: They tried to set my leg and they put it in plaster, but it didn't work.
sentences.zh: 他们试图为我的腿接骨并打了石膏，但没有成功。

sentences.en: So then they said, actually, after all that, we need to do surgery anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，好吧，经历了这一切之后，我们无论如何都得做手术。

sentences.en: I'm assuming there must have been a very lengthy period of rehab after this much work on your leg, Ciara.
sentences.zh: 基拉，我想在你腿上做了这么大手术之后，一定有一段非常漫长的康复期吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I mean, I couldn't walk at all for several months.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我有好几个月完全无法走路。

sentences.en: I was on crutches then afterwards for six months.
sentences.zh: 之后我拄了六个月的拐杖。

sentences.en: And there was very extensive physiotherapy and rehab and so on.
sentences.zh: 还有非常大量的物理治疗和康复训练等等。

sentences.en: It's three years later now and I do still have pain in my leg.
sentences.zh: 现在已经是三年后了，我的腿确实还在痛。

sentences.en: You know, it's much, much better.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，已经好太多了。

sentences.en: And I can, I don't limp anymore.
sentences.zh: 而且我，我不再瘸了。

sentences.en: Mostly I can walk fine, but I used to dance and I used to do things that I can't do anymore.
sentences.zh: 大体上我能正常走路，但我以前跳舞，还做过一些现在做不了的事情。

sentences.en: So, you know, it has had a lot of knock-on consequences in my life.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，它对我的生活产生了许多连锁反应。

sentences.en: More than I think, I think previously I would have used the expression, you know, somebody breaking a leg.
sentences.zh: 比我想象的要多，我想我以前可能会用这样的表达，你知道的，某人断了一条腿。

sentences.en: Oh, you might break a leg.
sentences.zh: 哦，你可能会断了一条腿。

sentences.en: And you think it's, you know, unpleasant, but not a huge deal.
sentences.zh: 你觉得这，你知道的，很不愉快，但并非什么大不了的事。

sentences.en: But it was quite life-altering in a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 但在许多方面，这确实改变了人生。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how the memories of this event have stayed with you.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这次事件的记忆是如何留在你身上的。

sentences.en: Have you been able to get back on a bike?
sentences.zh: 你还能重新骑上自行车吗？

sentences.en: Have you been able to, you know, go back to the place where the accident took place?
sentences.zh: 你还能，你知道的，回到事故发生的地方吗？

sentences.en: What's happened?
sentences.zh: 情况怎么样？

sentences.en: Yeah, so definitely the memories have stayed with me.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以记忆确实留在我身上了。

sentences.en: I'll find myself kind of repeatedly thinking about parts of it.
sentences.zh: 我会发现自己不知不觉地反复想起其中的某些部分。

sentences.en: In terms of getting back on a bike, I, well, of course I couldn't for a long time because I was physically, I would, I was totally unable to.
sentences.zh: 至于重新骑上自行车，我，嗯，当然很长一段时间都做不到，因为从身体上讲，我完全做不到。

sentences.en: I was in a wheelchair for a while and then I had, you know, crutches for a long time and, you know, but then maybe six, seven months after the accident, I did,
sentences.zh: 我坐了一段时间轮椅，然后，你知道的，拄了很长时间的拐杖，你知道的，但接着可能在事故发生六、七个月后，我确实，

sentences.en: I did get back on the bike.
sentences.zh: 我确实重新骑上了自行车。

sentences.en: I just said, right, I'll do a short cycle from, from my house down to my parents' house, which is not, you know, maybe a few miles.
sentences.zh: 我只是对自己说，好吧，我要进行一次短途骑行，从我家骑到我父母家，那不远，你知道的，可能也就几英里。

sentences.en: It's not very far.
sentences.zh: 不是很远。

sentences.en: And I did it and I was proud that I did it.
sentences.zh: 我做到了，而且我为自己做到了这一点感到骄傲。

sentences.en: But my heart was going, I just going like the clappers the whole time.
sentences.zh: 但我的心脏一直在狂跳，整个过程就像打鼓一样快。

sentences.en: And I found that I couldn't release my, I had this death grip on the handlebars and I couldn't release my hands from the handlebars enough to turn right.
sentences.zh: 我发现我无法松开，我对车把手有着一种死死抓住的铁钳般的握力，以至于我的手根本无法从车把手上松开来做出向右转的动作。

sentences.en: So, of course, we, we drive in Ireland on the left-hand side of the road.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，我们在爱尔兰是靠道路左侧行驶的。

sentences.en: So, turning left is, is easy enough.
sentences.zh: 所以，向左转是，是挺容易的。

sentences.en: You just stay on the side you are.
sentences.zh: 你只要呆在你原本的那侧就行。

sentences.en: Turning right involves crossing over the road.
sentences.zh: 向右转则需要穿过马路。

sentences.en: You have to indicate.
sentences.zh: 你必须打转向灯。

sentences.en: So, I did it to prove to myself that I could do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我这么做是为了向自己证明我能做到。

sentences.en: But it was such an anxiety-provoking experience that I, I, I couldn't, I feel there is a thing with,
sentences.zh: 但这是一种如此令人焦虑的经历，以至于我，我，我觉得有一件事……

sentences.en: with a lot of activities like cycling where you need to have a sort of illusion of invulnerability in order to do it.
sentences.zh: 比如骑车这种有很多活动的运动，为了完成它，你必须有一种刀枪不入的错觉。

sentences.en: And that illusion was completely shattered that I knew how vulnerable I was.
sentences.zh: 而那种错觉彻底破碎了，我意识到了自己有多脆弱。

sentences.en: And there was no getting around that.
sentences.zh: 这是无法回避的。

sentences.en: There was no pretending that this was a safe thing to do.
sentences.zh: 没法假装这是一件安全的事。

sentences.en: I no longer believed that it was in any way a safe thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我不再相信这在任何方面是一件安全的事了。

sentences.en: So, I never, I still have the bike and I still want to get back on it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我从未——我车还在，我也依然想重新骑上它。

sentences.en: But I've never gotten back to being able to cycle to work, for example.
sentences.zh: 但我再也回不到那种能骑车去上班的状态了，比如说。

sentences.en: And when you consider sort of going on the bike, when you consider the inconvenience of parking and you say, maybe I should bike today, what happens in your mind?
sentences.zh: 当你考虑骑车出行，当你想到停车的麻烦，然后对自己说，也许我今天应该骑车，你的脑子里会发生什么？

sentences.en: What does your mind say?
sentences.zh: 你的大脑会怎么说？

sentences.en: I don't think I've even really gotten to that stage.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我甚至还没真正到达那个阶段。

sentences.en: I think if I, if I was even to think about, you know, what I do it tomorrow, because I'd have to plan, I'd have to think, well, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想如果我，如果我甚至去想，你知道的，我明天要不要骑车，因为我得规划，我得思考，好吧，你知道的，

sentences.en: I'll pack the bike bag and I'll pump up the tires, you know, on the bike.
sentences.zh: 我要收拾车包，还要给轮胎打气，你知道的，就对那辆自行车。

sentences.en: And just straight away, I'm just like, no, it's, it's, there's always a thing.
sentences.zh: 然后马上，我就觉得，不，它，它，总会有各种状况。

sentences.en: It's particularly, I live in Ireland, it rains a lot.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我住在爱尔兰，雨水很多。

sentences.en: This is no surprise.
sentences.zh: 这并不奇怪。

sentences.en: If I look out the window and it looks like it might be wet, it might be rainy, the road might be slick.
sentences.zh: 如果我望向窗外，看起来可能会湿漉漉的、可能会下雨、路面可能会打滑。

sentences.en: Absolutely no way.
sentences.zh: 绝对没门。

sentences.en: The thought of getting on the bike is, is, is, is really very frightening.
sentences.zh: 一想到要骑上自行车，就，就，就，真的非常害怕。

sentences.en: I start to feel very anxious about it.
sentences.zh: 我开始为此感到极度焦虑。

sentences.en: And so even if I'm driving and I see people, you know, cyclists weaving around, I get so anxious on their behalf.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使我在开车，看到人们，你知道的，骑车人在车流中穿梭，我都会为他们感到十分焦虑。

sentences.en: What if they slipped?
sentences.zh: 万一他们滑倒了呢？

sentences.en: What if they fell?
sentences.zh: 万一他们摔倒了呢？

sentences.en: What if they got knocked down?
sentences.zh: 万一他们被撞倒了呢？

sentences.en: What if they had an accident?
sentences.zh: 万一他们出了事故呢？

sentences.en: That it is, it is, it's absorbing a good amount of my attention.
sentences.zh: 这，这，这占据了我相当大的一部分注意力。

sentences.en: You mentioned a second ago that what happened at the hospital was also in some ways very difficult.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到，在医院发生的事情在某些方面也非常艰难。

sentences.en: Well, that in some ways that you continue to have these memories.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某些方面，你会不断浮现这些记忆。

sentences.en: Are you still bothered by those memories of what happened when, when you received ketamine and when you were in the, in the hospital?
sentences.zh: 你依然会被那些记忆困扰吗？关于当你注射了氯胺酮以及你在，在医院时的经历？

sentences.en: Yes, to a certain extent.
sentences.zh: 是的，在某种程度上会。

sentences.en: But then I had a strange experience maybe a year and a half ago.
sentences.zh: 但后来我在大概一年半前有了一次奇怪的经历。

sentences.en: So maybe again, about a year and a half after the accident, I had laser eye surgery.
sentences.zh: 所以也许还是大约在事故发生一年半后，我做了激光矫视手术。

sentences.en: It only takes about 10 minutes and it's not painful.
sentences.zh: 只需要大约10分钟，而且不痛。

sentences.en: They put, you know, anesthetic eye drops into your eyes.
sentences.zh: 他们会在你的眼睛里滴入，你知道的，麻醉眼药水。

sentences.en: But obviously your eyes are open for the surgery and there's, you know, a laser coming in and doing things.
sentences.zh: 但很显然，手术时你的眼睛是睁开的，而且你知道的，会有激光进来做一些操作。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of pressure on your eye.
sentences.zh: 你的眼睛会受到很大的压力。

sentences.en: And when they're doing that, you see strange things.
sentences.zh: 当他们这样做时，你会看到奇异的景象。

sentences.en: Like it looks like, kind of like a tunnel.
sentences.zh: 比如看起来，有点像一个隧道。

sentences.en: You know, you have that kind of vibe of things looking like, like things are coming away, shooting away from you or coming towards you like they're down a tunnel.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，会有那种氛围，感觉东西看起来，就像有东西从你身边飞射而去，或者朝你冲过来，就像它们在一个隧道里一样。

sentences.en: And I had this almost flashback to that ketamine experience where I told you it felt like I was being compressed and squeezed down a tunnel.
sentences.zh: 我几乎有了对那次氯胺酮经历的闪回，我跟你说过，当时感觉自己像是在被压缩，被挤压进一个隧道里。

sentences.en: And it was just the visual elements of that gave me this kind of reaction.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是那些视觉元素就让我产生了这种反应。

sentences.en: And I knew that's what was happening at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我很清楚发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I didn't have a panic attack or anything, but I was aware that I was like, God, this is like that.
sentences.zh: 我没有恐慌发作或什么的，但我意识到自己在想，天哪，这太像那次了。

sentences.en: And it made it very, very unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 这让人感觉非常非常不愉快。

sentences.en: And it felt like a long 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 这10分钟感觉格外漫长。

sentences.en: All of us want to have a sharp memory.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都希望能拥有敏锐的记忆。

sentences.en: But Keira's painful memories of her bike accident raise an important question.
sentences.zh: 但琪拉关于车祸的痛苦记忆引发了一个重要问题。

sentences.en: Is a sharp memory always a good thing?
sentences.zh: 敏锐的记忆就一定是好事吗？

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维达坦姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维达坦姆。

sentences.en: Most of us wish we could remember things better.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都希望自己的记忆力能更好一些。

sentences.en: We think of forgetting as a flaw.
sentences.zh: 我们把遗忘视为一种缺陷。

sentences.en: But being able to forget some things can be a blessing.
sentences.zh: 但能够忘掉一些事情其实是一种福气。

sentences.en: At University College Dublin, psychologist Keira Green cites the example of a woman with an unusual ability.
sentences.zh: 在都柏林大学学院，心理学家琪拉·格林举了一个拥有非凡能力的女性的例子。

sentences.en: So Jill Price is a woman who's very well known because she has an extremely rare condition that's called highly superior autobiographical memory,
sentences.zh: 吉尔·普莱斯是一位非常著名的女性，因为她患有一种极其罕见的病症，被称为超常自传体记忆，

sentences.en: which is usually abbreviated as HSAM.
sentences.zh: 通常简称为 HSAM。

sentences.en: And what it is, is a really extraordinary memory for the events of your own life.
sentences.zh: 这种能力指的是对你自身生活中的事件拥有真正非凡的记忆力。

sentences.en: So somebody with HSAM, like somebody like Jill, for example, will be able to tell you in enormous detail about all the incidents of their lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，拥有 HSAM 的人，比如吉尔这样的人，能够向你极其详细地讲述他们生活中的所有经历。

sentences.en: Like somebody who you might be able to say, tell me what the weather was like on the 30th of September 1998.
sentences.zh: 就像你可能会对某个人说，告诉我1998年9月30日的天气是什么样的。

sentences.en: And most of us would go, how on earth would I possibly know that?
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都会想，我怎么可能知道那是什么样的？

sentences.en: But somebody with HSAM, someone like Jill, would say, oh yeah, I remember.
sentences.zh: 但拥有 HSAM 的人，像吉尔这样的人，会说，哦，是的，我记得。

sentences.en: It was really sunny, but the clouds came over at about three o'clock.
sentences.zh: 那天阳光明媚，但大约三点钟时云层压了过来。

sentences.en: We thought for a while it was going to rain, but then it didn't.
sentences.zh: 我们有一会儿以为要下雨了，但后来没下。

sentences.en: And I was hanging out with my friends and my friend picked me up and then we went off down to the shopping centre and we hung out outside Claire's accessories.
sentences.zh: 当时我和朋友们在一起，我朋友抱起了我，然后我们一起去了购物中心，在克莱尔饰品店外面闲逛。

sentences.en: And my friend was thinking about getting her ears pierced.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友在考虑去打耳洞。

sentences.en: And, you know, would be able to give you this extremely detailed blow-by-blow account of their own personal experiences.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，能够向你提供这种极其详细、逐字逐句的个人经历描述。

sentences.en: So Jill Price wrote a memoir about her condition and in the memoir, she tells a story about something that happened to her when she was a child.
sentences.zh: 所以吉尔·普莱斯写了一本关于她这种病症的回忆录，在回忆录中，她讲述了她小时候发生的一件事。

sentences.en: Tell me the story, Ciara.
sentences.zh: 讲讲这个故事吧，琪拉。

sentences.en: So she tells the story that her dad used to work as the agent for Jim Henson, who, of course, was the creator of the Muppets and, you know, the brain behind Sesame Street.
sentences.zh: 她讲述的故事是，她父亲曾担任吉姆·汉森的经纪人，而吉姆·汉森当然就是《布偶秀》的创造者，你知道的，也是《芝麻街》背后的灵魂人物。

sentences.en: And, you know, he would tell all these kind of stories about, you know, to the family and everything, all about Sesame Street and about Jim Henson and how incredible it was.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他会给家人讲各种各样的故事，关于《芝麻街》的，关于吉姆·汉森的，以及这一切有多么不可思议。

sentences.en: And at the time, Jill was very young.
sentences.zh: 当时吉尔还很小。

sentences.en: She was in nursery school.
sentences.zh: 她还在上幼儿园。

sentences.en: But her dad arranged for her whole class to go on a field trip to Jim Henson's studio where all of the puppets were created.
sentences.zh: 但她父亲安排了她全班去吉姆·汉森的工作室进行一次实地考察，那里是所有木偶诞生的地方。

sentences.en: And this, you know, they've talked it up for ages.
sentences.zh: 而且这个，你知道的，他们已经谈论了好久了。

sentences.en: And this is something, of course, that they were all really, really looking forward to it.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是他们所有人都非常非常期待的一件事。

sentences.en: But when the day came around for the field trip, Jill was sick.
sentences.zh: 但当实地考察的那天到来时，吉尔生病了。

sentences.en: She had tonsillitis.
sentences.zh: 她得了扁桃体炎。

sentences.en: So she wasn't able to go.
sentences.zh: 所以她去不了。

sentences.en: And, of course, being very, very young, she didn't understand that, you know, her father had already committed to this and had already committed to take the whole class with her.
sentences.zh: 当然，由于年纪非常非常小，她并不理解，你知道的，她父亲已经承诺了这件事，并且已经承诺带着全班同学一起去。

sentences.en: So they had to go ahead.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须继续行程。

sentences.en: Without his own daughter, they had to go ahead and run the trip.
sentences.zh: 在没有他自己女儿的情况下，他们不得不继续前往并完成这次参观。

sentences.en: And she was devastated.
sentences.zh: 她伤心欲绝。

sentences.en: Couldn't understand why he was doing this, taking all of her friends, leaving her behind.
sentences.zh: 无法理解他为什么要这么做，带着她所有的朋友，把她一个人留在后面。

sentences.en: And even though she had tonsillitis, so she had a really sore throat, she stood, you know, screaming at the top of her lungs,
sentences.zh: 尽管她患有扁桃体炎，喉咙痛得厉害，她还是站在那里，你知道的，声嘶力竭地尖叫，

sentences.en: screaming at her parents so they were not letting them go.
sentences.zh: 向父母尖叫，就是不让他们去。

sentences.en: And she says, you know, that it was a small thing in retrospect, but that when every time she thinks about it,
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道的，回想起来这只是一件小事，但每当她想起这件事，

sentences.en: she still feels this overwhelming sense of disappointment every time she sees the Muppets.
sentences.zh: 每当她看到《布偶秀》时，她依然会感到这种铺天盖地的失望感。

sentences.en: So every time you see a Muppets Christmas Carol, you're brought back to this moment of not just a rose-tinted view of, oh, ha, ha,
sentences.zh: 所以每次你看到《布偶秀圣诞颂歌》，你都会被带回到那个时刻，不仅带着一层玫瑰色的滤镜去想，哦，哈哈，

sentences.en: this is a funny thing that happened to me as a child, but really, like, almost being right back there again and feeling it as though she's right there in the moment.
sentences.zh: 这是我小时候发生的一件趣事，而是真的，几乎就像重新回到了那个现场，那种感觉就像她此刻正身临其境一样。

sentences.en: Now, because she has this extraordinary memory, this extraordinary autobiographical recall for things, she remembers very vivid details about what happened that day.
sentences.zh: 现在，由于她拥有这种非凡的记忆力，这种对事情非凡的自传式回忆能力，她能记住那天发生的事情中非常生动的细节。

sentences.en: She remembers hearing her mother walking away from her and hearing the sound of her mother's heels as they walk away from her.
sentences.zh: 她记得听到母亲走开的声音，以及母亲高跟鞋离她远去的脚步声。

sentences.en: Really, really detailed.
sentences.zh: 真的非常非常详细。

sentences.en: Now, what's striking, of course, is that when things happened to us many years ago, in time, our memories start to fade.
sentences.zh: 现在，引人注目的是，当然，当很多年前的事情发生时，随着时间推移，我们的记忆开始褪色。

sentences.en: We start to forget details of it, but that seems like that's not the case for Jill.
sentences.zh: 我们开始忘记其中的细节，但对吉尔来说似乎并非如此。

sentences.en: No, so it's actually, it is very unusual.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以实际上，这非常不寻常。

sentences.en: Whereas, say, my memory of a childhood event might be very, very fuzzy, very foggy.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，比方说我对童年某次经历的记忆可能会非常非常模糊，非常朦胧。

sentences.en: I might remember kind of a core detail of that event, but I might not remember how I got there or what happened afterwards or what I was wearing.
sentences.zh: 我可能还记得那件事的核心细节，但我可能不记得我是怎么去的，或者后来发生了什么，或者我当时穿的是什么。

sentences.en: All of those really, really clear details, those are still very vivid in Jill's memory.
sentences.zh: 所有那些非常非常清晰的细节，在吉尔的记忆里依然十分生动。

sentences.en: I remember a time when I was running around.
sentences.zh: 我还记得自己到处奔跑的一段时光。

sentences.en: I must have been 12 or 13.
sentences.zh: 我当时大概12或13岁。

sentences.en: It was dark.
sentences.zh: 天很黑。

sentences.en: I think I was in a parking lot somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时在某个停车场里。

sentences.en: I tripped and fell.
sentences.zh: 我绊倒并摔了下去。

sentences.en: I landed very hard on my finger.
sentences.zh: 我的手指重重地着地。

sentences.en: I broke my finger.
sentences.zh: 我的手指骨折了。

sentences.en: It was very painful at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时疼得厉害。

sentences.en: But now when I look back on it, you know, I look back on it and say, you know, that's what being a kid was.
sentences.zh: 但现在我回想起这件事时，你知道的，我回过头去看并会说，你知道的，这就是当孩子时的样子。

sentences.en: You know, you ran around, you did silly things, and you had injuries.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你会四处奔跑，做一些傻事，然后受点伤。

sentences.en: I no longer remember the pain.
sentences.zh: 我已经不记得那种疼痛了。

sentences.en: I don't remember the details.
sentences.zh: 我不记得细节了。

sentences.en: To be honest, I'm not even sure which finger was actually hurt anymore.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我甚至不确定到底是哪根手指受过伤了。

sentences.en: But with Jill, because she has this detailed memory, the memory is also painful in a way for her that it's not for me.
sentences.zh: 但对吉尔来说，因为她拥有这种详细的记忆，对她而言，这种记忆也是痛苦的，而这对我来说并不是这样的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: So, like, she's, a lot of the time really what's happening here is that she's constantly reliving these same experiences and kind of perseverating on them and thinking about them.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像，她，很多时候这里实际发生的情况是，她一直在不断地重温这些相同的经历，并对它们反复琢磨、念念不忘。

sentences.en: And then it does mean then that you're not able to let some of these things go.
sentences.zh: 这就意味着你无法放下其中的一些事情。

sentences.en: So, we often tend to think of this kind of really extraordinary memory as being an extra gift, that it's this extra, like, wonderful thing that you have, this skill that you have.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们往往倾向于认为这种真正非凡的记忆力是一种额外的天赋，是某种额外的、美妙的东西，是你拥有的某种技能。

sentences.en: And in some ways, of course, it is.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，当然它确实是。

sentences.en: And a lot of people who have this condition or, you know, who have this ability think of it as being wonderful.
sentences.zh: 许多患有这种病症或，你知道的，拥有这种能力的人也认为它是美妙的。

sentences.en: But there are significant downsides.
sentences.zh: 但其中也有重大的负面影响。

sentences.en: And one other way of thinking about this is that it's not so much a great ability to remember as it is an inability to forget.
sentences.zh: 从另一个角度来看，与其说这是一种强大的记忆能力，不如说这是一种无法遗忘的无能为力。

sentences.en: So, Jill Price doesn't just remember this one childhood event.
sentences.zh: 所以，吉尔·普莱斯不仅记得这一个童年事件。

sentences.en: She remembers other things in her life.
sentences.zh: 她还记得生活中的其他事情。

sentences.en: Tell me the story about her husband, Jim, and what happened to him, Ciara.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲她丈夫吉姆的故事，以及他身上发生了什么，琪拉。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的，是的。

sentences.en: So, in the book, Jill talks a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以在书中，吉尔谈了很多。

sentences.en: She firstly talks a lot about how she met her husband, Jim.
sentences.zh: 她首先谈了很多关于她是如何遇到她的丈夫吉姆的。

sentences.en: And, you know, they had been, had a kind of a long-distance relationship at firSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们一开始经历了一种长距离的恋爱关系。

sentences.en: And then when they met, they had this really, really strong connection and, you know, fell very deeply in love and got married and, you know, lived together.
sentences.zh: 然后当他们见面时，他们有着非常非常深厚的联系，你知道的，深深地相爱了，结了婚，你知道的，生活在了一起。

sentences.en: Ciara had this, you know, from her recollection, had this wonderful marriage.
sentences.zh: 在琪拉的记忆中，你知道的，她拥有这段美满的婚姻。

sentences.en: But there is this extremely tragic end to it, which is that only after only two years of marriage, when Jim was only 42, he died.
sentences.zh: 但这段婚姻有一个极其悲惨的结局，那就是仅仅在结婚两年后，当吉姆只有42岁时，他去世了。

sentences.en: He had very severe diabetes and he suffered a stroke as a result of that and died as a result after several days in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 他患有非常严重的糖尿病，并因此引发了中风，在医院度过几天后不幸离世。

sentences.en: Now, one of the things that's striking is that because Jill had such good memory, she could remember many of the good times in great detail,
sentences.zh: 现在，令人触动的一点是，因为吉尔的记忆力太好了，她能非常详细地记住许多美好的时光，

sentences.en: perhaps in much better detail than many of us could have remembered it.
sentences.zh: 也许比我们大多数人所能记住的要详细得多。

sentences.en: She remembered when she first met Jim, you know, that first night together, what their wedding day was like.
sentences.zh: 她记得她第一次见到吉姆时，你知道的，在一起的那个第一夜晚，他们的婚礼是什么样的。

sentences.en: She remembered the good times in extraordinary detail.
sentences.zh: 她以非凡的细节记住了那些美好的时光。

sentences.en: But that also meant that she remembered the tragic end in excruciating detail.
sentences.zh: 但这也就意味着她以极其痛苦的细节记住了那个悲惨的结局。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: And I mean, of course, many people listening might be saying, well, I remember my wedding day as well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，许多听众可能会说，我也记得我的婚礼。

sentences.en: But I think the thing is that it's not just these big key events that she remembers.
sentences.zh: 但我认为关键在于，她记住的不只是这些重大的关键事件。

sentences.en: It's also just everyday things.
sentences.zh: 还有那些日常生活中的琐事。

sentences.en: And she will remember not just our first date was great, but every detail of it in extraordinary clarity.
sentences.zh: 她不仅会记得我们的第一次约会很棒，而且会以非凡的清晰度记住其中的每一个细节。

sentences.en: But yes, towards the end then as well, she also cannot allow those terrible memories of Jim's illness and death to fade.
sentences.zh: 但同样的，到了最后阶段，她也无法让那些关于吉姆生病和去世的可可怖记忆褪色。

sentences.en: So she describes in really great detail how, you know, her father came home and told her that Jim had collapsed at work and then they're driving to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 所以她极其详细地描述了，你知道的，她父亲回家告诉她吉姆在工作时晕倒了，然后他们开车赶往医院。

sentences.en: And she goes through in this just exhaustive detail every phone call she made to the nurse.
sentences.zh: 她以这种详尽无遗的细节回顾了她给护士打的每一个电话。

sentences.en: And then the nurse is telling her this.
sentences.zh: 然后护士把这些告诉了她。

sentences.en: And then, you know, all these details of the drive to the hospital and then, you know, what the doctors were, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，去医院路上的所有细节，然后，你知道的，医生们，你知道的，

sentences.en: this horrible situation where he was in critical care for days.
sentences.zh: 那种可怕的情况是他在重症监护室呆了好几天。

sentences.en: And then eventually the doctors had to tell her that they had to turn off the life support machines.
sentences.zh: 最后医生不得不告诉她，他们必须关闭生命维持系统。

sentences.en: The fact of this terrible thing happening is something that everyone would remember.
sentences.zh: 发生这种可怕事情的事实是每个人都会记得的。

sentences.en: And nobody's going to have forgotten that their husband died so tragically.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人会忘记他们的丈夫死得如此悲惨。

sentences.en: But it's every little detail of it.
sentences.zh: 但这是其中的每一个微小细节。

sentences.en: And she says that even like every time now, years and years later, she can't drive down that road where they drove to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 她说，甚至现在，多年后的每一次，她都无法开车经过他们去医院的那条路。

sentences.en: Because every vivid little detail of that drive to the hospital is there as it comes back.
sentences.zh: 因为去医院那一程的每一个生动小细节都历历在目，挥之不去。

sentences.en: And they don't fade with time.
sentences.zh: 而且它们不会随时间消逝。

sentences.en: You know, we have that cliche that time is a great healer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们常说“时间是最好的疗伤圣药”这样一个陈词滥调。

sentences.en: And we do tend to see that, that over time, our negative memories tend to fade and we tend to hold on more to the positive memories.
sentences.zh: 我们也确实倾向于看到这一点：随着时间的推移，我们的负面记忆往往会消逝，而我们会更多地记住正面记忆。

sentences.en: Now, there are exceptions.
sentences.zh: 当然，也有例外。

sentences.en: But Jill's memory really doesn't seem to discriminate.
sentences.zh: 但吉尔的记忆似乎并不分门别类或有所选择。

sentences.en: She holds on to all of those details, whether or not they're still relevant, whether or not they're useful to her.
sentences.zh: 她记住了所有这些细节，无论它们是否仍然相关，无论对她是否有用。

sentences.en: However, she's still holding on to all of them.
sentences.zh: 然而，她依然牢牢记住所有这一切。

sentences.en: Kira, say more about this idea.
sentences.zh: 基拉，请多谈谈这个想法。

sentences.en: I think when many of us think about forgetting, we think about forgetting as a flaw.
sentences.zh: 我认为，当我们许多人想到“遗忘”时，我们会认为遗忘是一种缺陷。

sentences.en: You know, I find myself forgetting things all the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我发现自己一直在忘事。

sentences.en: And whenever I forget things, I'm so upset with myself.
sentences.zh: 每当我忘事时，我都会对自己感到非常懊恼。

sentences.en: And I say, you know, I used to have a fantastic memory and now my memory is failing me.
sentences.zh: 我会说，你知道，我以前的记忆力好得不得了，而现在我的记忆力大不如前了。

sentences.en: It's not good.
sentences.zh: 这可不好。

sentences.en: I worry if I have a disorder of some kind.
sentences.zh: 我甚至担心自己是不是得了某种毛病。

sentences.en: Talk about this idea that in some ways we get it profoundly wrong when we think about forgetting as a flaw.
sentences.zh: 谈谈这种观点：在某种程度上，当我们把遗忘视为一种缺陷时，我们大错特错了。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I think the first thing to note is that forgetting is actually a fundamental component of memory.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为首先要注意的是，遗忘其实是记忆的一个基本组成部分。

sentences.en: We tend to think of forgetting almost as the flip side of memory.
sentences.zh: 我们往往把遗忘看作是记忆的对立面。

sentences.en: And that memory is the positive, what we're supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 仿佛记忆是积极的、是我们应该做到的。

sentences.en: And then forgetting is the thing that the accidental thing that happens.
sentences.zh: 而遗忘则是偶然发生的事情。

sentences.en: But that's really not the case.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Like forgetting is a fundamental element of what happens in our memory processes.
sentences.zh: 遗忘实际上是我们记忆过程中发生的一个基本要素。

sentences.en: I think a lot of the problem here comes in that when we tend to make the mistake of thinking that our memories act like a computer system,
sentences.zh: 我认为这里的大部分问题在于，我们往往会错误地认为我们的记忆就像一个计算机系统，

sentences.en: that we should be able to just file away information and then it will stay in that same place.
sentences.zh: 我们应该能够把信息归档，然后它就会停留在同一个地方。

sentences.en: And then later on, we should be able to retrieve that information and we pull it back exactly the same way it was before.
sentences.zh: 然后过一段时间，我们应该能够检索这些信息，并以完全和以前一模一样的方式把它调取出来。

sentences.en: And if we had a computer where we went to go and retrieve a file and the file wasn't there, it had been accidentally deleted, we'd be disgusted.
sentences.zh: 如果我们有一台电脑，当我去检索一个文件却发现文件不在了，它被意外删除了，我们会感到气愤。

sentences.en: That's not what a computer is supposed to do, right?
sentences.zh: 电脑本来就不该是这样的，对吧？

sentences.en: A computer is supposed to retain this perfect record of information as we recorded it.
sentences.zh: 电脑应该保留我们录入时的完美信息记录。

sentences.en: That's not what our memories do.
sentences.zh: 但我们的记忆不是这样的。

sentences.en: That's not how our memories work.
sentences.zh: 我们的记忆不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: Rather than thinking of memory as being this kind of passive process where we just file information away and then it just stays there,
sentences.zh: 与其把记忆看作是一种被动过程——我们把信息归档然后它就留在那儿，

sentences.en: memory is actually this really active process where we're kind of actively engaging in our memories.
sentences.zh: 不如说记忆实际上是一个非常主动的过程，我们在其中积极地参与我们的记忆。

sentences.en: We engage in actively constructing and reconstructing our memories and we change the way our memories are stored in our brains.
sentences.zh: 我们积极地构建和重构我们的记忆，并改变记忆在大脑中的储存方式。

sentences.en: And part of that process is that forgetting is a kind of a natural sort of digestion process in memory,
sentences.zh: 这个过程的一部分就是，遗忘其实是记忆中一种自然的消化过程，

sentences.en: that we have lots and lots of different events in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们在生活中经历着许许多多不同的事件。

sentences.en: And one of the really key things that our memories do and that forgetting helps us do essentially is to identify the gist of those memories.
sentences.zh: 我们的记忆所做的关键事情之一——从根本上说，遗忘帮我们做到的事情之一——就是提炼这些记忆的要旨。

sentences.en: So, like for example, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，比方说，对吧？

sentences.en: Like imagine every day probably you eat breakfast, okay?
sentences.zh: 比如想象一下，你大概每天都要吃早餐，对吧？

sentences.en: And probably most days you eat more or less the same thing for breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且可能大多数日子里，你早餐吃的东西都大同小异。

sentences.en: Maybe you eat something different on the weekends than you do the weekdays, okay?
sentences.zh: 也许周末吃的东西和工作日有点不一样，好吗？

sentences.en: But probably you eat the same thing more or less every morning.
sentences.zh: 但大概每天早上你吃的都差不多。

sentences.en: You could, if you think of that computer metaphor, you could imagine that for every single day of your life,
sentences.zh: 如果你套用那个电脑比喻，你可以想象，在你生命的每一天里，

sentences.en: you should have a perfect, veridical recollection of exactly what you ate for breakfast,
sentences.zh: 你都应该对你早餐吃了什么、

sentences.en: how you poured out the cornflakes, how you poured out the milk, how you sat down at the table, picked up your spoon,
sentences.zh: 你是怎么倒玉米片的、怎么倒牛奶、怎么在桌旁坐下、怎么拿起汤匙，

sentences.en: how many bites you ate, how many times you chewed each bite.
sentences.zh: 你吃了多少口、每一口咀嚼了多少次，有着完美、真实的回忆。

sentences.en: But honestly, what a waste of time to remember all of these things in such detail.
sentences.zh: 但老实说，把所有这些细节都记住，简直是浪费时间。

sentences.en: Really, all you really need to know is to sort of condense all of that information into,
sentences.zh: 其实，你真正需要做的，只是把所有这些信息浓缩成：

sentences.en: usually I eat cornflakes for breakfast, okay?
sentences.zh: 我通常早餐吃玉米片，对吧？

sentences.en: And then sometimes when something a little bit different happens,
sentences.zh: 然后，有时当发生了一些稍微不同的事情时，

sentences.en: then we need to be able to remember that.
sentences.zh: 我们需要能够记住它。

sentences.en: Like, well, we ran out of milk this morning, so I had toast instead.
sentences.zh: 比如，今天早上我们牛奶喝完了，所以我改吃吐司了。

sentences.en: I must remember to go to the shop and buy milk.
sentences.zh: 我必须记得去商店买牛奶。

sentences.en: But most of the time, remembering all of these very repetitive events in our lives in this perfect individual detail,
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候，把我们生活中所有这些高度重复的事件以完美的个人细节一一记住，

sentences.en: it's actually a really inefficient way of storing information.
sentences.zh: 实际上是一种非常低效的信息储存方式。

sentences.en: Instead, we kind of condense that information down and we pull out the gist of those kind of repeated, continuous events.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们会把这些信息浓缩，并提取出那些重复、连续事件的要旨。

sentences.en: So if you can't do that, if you're not able to kind of essentially leave some of those details behind you,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你做不到这一点，如果你基本上无法将其中一些细节抛在脑后，

sentences.en: then what you're going to have more trouble doing is identifying the gist,
sentences.zh: 那么你就会发现在提炼要旨、

sentences.en: identifying the commonalities among all of those different events.
sentences.zh: 找出所有这些不同事件之间的共同点时遇到更多困难。

sentences.en: You know, it's so striking, Kira, because I think when most of us think of memory,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这太令人震撼了，基拉，因为我认为当我们大多数人想到记忆时，

sentences.en: not just in our individual lives, but also I think in our social lives,
sentences.zh: 不仅在我们的个人生活中，而且在我们的社会生活中，

sentences.en: we think of forgetting as almost being something that is bad.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎把遗忘看作是一件坏事。

sentences.en: I mean, if you think about courtroom settings, for example,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你想想法庭审判的场景，

sentences.en: we think about people who don't remember where they were or what they were doing at the time of a crime
sentences.zh: 我们会认为那些记不清在犯罪发生时自己身在何处或在做什麽的人

sentences.en: as being potentially suspicious or even guilty.
sentences.zh: 具有潜在的可疑性甚至有罪。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: I think, again, it comes back to that idea that we really have these very unrealistic expectations
sentences.zh: 我认为，这又回到了那个观点，即我们对我们的记忆能做什么或应该做什么，

sentences.en: of what our memories can or should do.
sentences.zh: 确实抱有过高且不切实际的期望。

sentences.en: And we tend to hold, to a certain extent ourselves,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们对自己，

sentences.en: but really other people to very unrealistic standards regarding their memory.
sentences.zh: 但实际上对其他人，也往往抱有关于记忆的不切实际的标准。

sentences.en: And we tend to assume, for example, and there's lots of evidence of this,
sentences.zh: 我们往往会假设——有大量证据表明这一点——

sentences.en: that in, for example, forensic or legal settings, as you've said,
sentences.zh: 例如在法医或法律场合，正如你所说，

sentences.en: we tend to assume that if someone's memory changes or has gaps in it,
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于假设如果某人的记忆发生变化或出现空白，

sentences.en: that they're hiding something or that they're lying.
sentences.zh: 就说明他们在隐瞒什么或者在撒谎。

sentences.en: That if their memory of an event changes, that shows that they're lying about that event
sentences.zh: 如果他们对某件事的记忆改变了，这就表明他们在对这件事撒谎，

sentences.en: and that they can't be trusted.
sentences.zh: 因此是不可信的。

sentences.en: If there's a gap in their memory, maybe they're lying.
sentences.zh: 如果他们的记忆有空白，也许他们在撒谎。

sentences.en: Maybe they can't be trusted.
sentences.zh: 也许他们不可信。

sentences.en: There's something going on where, in fact, that is completely normal.
sentences.zh: 总觉得有什么不对劲，而事实上，这完全是正常的。

sentences.en: And if somebody is actually able to give you this perfect,
sentences.zh: 如果有人真的能向你提供这种完美、

sentences.en: clear description of what happened to them,
sentences.zh: 清晰的描述，说明他们身上发生了什么，

sentences.en: a lot of that is going to have been essentially reconstructed and rebuilt.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分基本上都是经过重构和重建的。

sentences.en: So, in fact, even the story I told you earlier on about my accident,
sentences.zh: 所以，事实上，甚至我刚才跟你讲的关于我的事故的故事，

sentences.en: and in particular, the story I told you about the incident with the ketamine and so on,
sentences.zh: 尤其是关于氯胺酮等事件的故事，

sentences.en: I was literally under the influence of drugs.
sentences.zh: 我当时确实是在药物影响下。

sentences.en: I do not have a clear memory of that,
sentences.zh: 我对那件事没有清晰的记忆，

sentences.en: but I have a reconstructed memory of how I remember it having happened.
sentences.zh: 但我对事情发生的经过有一个重建的记忆。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that that's actually necessarily an accurate representation of what happened.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着这一定是对所发生事情的准确再现。

sentences.en: It's my reality, but it doesn't necessarily correspond to external reality.
sentences.zh: 这是我的现实，但它不一定对应外部现实。

sentences.en: In some ways, Kira, there's a famous Maya Angelou quote that sums up very well what you were just saying.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，基拉，玛雅·安杰卢有一句名言很好地总结了你刚才所说的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, she says that, so people will forget what you said,
sentences.zh: 是的，她说，人们会忘记你所说的话，

sentences.en: people will forget what you did, but people will never forget how you made them feel.
sentences.zh: 人们会忘记你所做的事，但人们永远不会忘记你带给他们的感受。

sentences.en: And I think that really is that idea, again, of that core aspect of what it is
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实体现了那个观点，也就是我们试图从事件中记住的东西的

sentences.en: that we're trying to remember from events.
sentences.zh: 核心本质是什么。

sentences.en: So, I remember that my bike accident was frightening and terrifying.
sentences.zh: 所以，我记得我的自行车事故令人害怕和恐惧。

sentences.en: But, you know, did I cross the white line before the back wheel went out or not?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，在后轮失控之前，我到底有没有越过白线？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I could probably, if I thought about that long enough,
sentences.zh: 如果我想得够久，我大概

sentences.en: I would construct a memory in which I would tell you with certainty that I had,
sentences.zh: 会构建一段记忆，并在其中信誓旦旦地告诉你，我确实

sentences.en: you know, I was on the correct side of the white line.
sentences.zh: 在白线的正确一侧。

sentences.en: But there's no guarantee that that memory is accurate, okay?
sentences.zh: 但这并不能保证这段记忆是准确的，对吧？

sentences.en: But what I can tell you with confidence is how I feel about it
sentences.zh: 但我能满怀信心地告诉你的是我的感受，

sentences.en: and about that core emotional content of the memory.
sentences.zh: 以及这段记忆的核心情感内容。

sentences.en: You know, I also find it a little amusing that people remember that quote as coming from Maya Angelou
sentences.zh: 你知道，我也觉得有点滑稽的是，人们把这句名言归功于玛雅·安杰卢，

sentences.en: when, in fact, it probably predated her.
sentences.zh: 而事实上，它可能比她出现得更早。

sentences.en: So, the feeling that it was from Maya Angelou sticks in our head
sentences.zh: 所以，“这句话出自玛雅·安杰卢”的感觉深深印在我们的脑海中，

sentences.en: more than the fact of whether it actually was from her or not.
sentences.zh: 胜过了它是否真的出自她之手这一事实。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, I think that's the case with a lot of famous quotes is that they get,
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我认为许多名言都是这样，它们被，

sentences.en: I mean, I'd say 90% of quotes on the internet are attributed to Oscar Wilde.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我会说互联网上90%的名言都被归功于奥斯卡·王尔德。

sentences.en: And I mean, the man said a lot of things, but he didn't say everything.
